name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CosmosEscape: Taking over Every Database in Azure Cosmos DB
items.dek: Authentication bypass in Azure Cosmos DB allows account takeover across all databases via connection string exposure in error messages.
items.unproven: whether Wiz disclosed responsibly before publication; whether Microsoft has issued patches or workarounds for existing deployments

items.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents
items.dek: Concurrent audio prompt injections using instruction augmentation and scenario concealment achieve 69% attack success on Gemini 3 Pro and GPT-4o-audio.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to audio-in multimodal agents; does not test whether agents in SDLC pipelines (code review, architecture analysis) inherit the same vulnerability.

items.title: Not In My Git Yard: Catching Backdoors at Commit and Release Time
items.dek: Lily integrates backdoor detection into CI pipelines and release workflows via trigger-aware fuzzing on Linux distributions.
items.unproven: false-positive rate on real-world codebases; whether trigger space is sufficiently compressed to scale to large projects.

items.title: CVE-2026-20316 — Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Use of Hard-coded Password Vulnerability
items.dek: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC). Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 1 August.

items.title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
items.dek: Black-box extraction of inference-time harnesses in LLM multi-agent systems leaks operational coordination logic and decision patterns.
items.unproven: Framework and threat model presented; no measurements of what fraction of real AMAS harnesses are extractable or whether defenses exist.

items.title: Safeguards Based on Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety for LLMs
items.dek: LLM safety guardrails decide before seeing downstream use; copyable context cannot guarantee safety without hard-to-copy credentials.
items.unproven: whether credential-based mitigations are implementable within existing commercial LLM guardrail tooling.

items.title: Don't Trust the AI Ecosystem: Analyzing Privacy Leakage in Compromised Open-Source Components
items.dek: GradLock embeds pixel-perfect training data into model weights via compromised supply chains, extracting with near-lossless fidelity.
items.unproven: robustness against federated learning or other gradient obfuscation; detection feasibility during code review or model inspection.

items.title: Send and Pretend: Exploiting Transcript Consistency Issues in End-to-End Encrypted Group Chats
items.dek: Signal, iMessage, Threema, and WhatsApp allow group members to send inconsistent transcripts without UI warning; equivocation vectors span protocol fallback and pairwise channels.
items.unproven: scope limited to named messengers; unclear whether patches or mitigations exist; no disclosure timeline or vendor response reported

items.title: SecRespond: Benchmarking AI Agents for Real-World Post-Compromise Incident Response
items.dek: First benchmark for LLM agent evaluation on post-compromise incident response across 10 cyber ranges and 23 models.
items.unproven: whether performance on constructed cyber ranges predicts real IR outcomes; whether results generalize beyond the tested LLM families.

items.title: Graph Is the Verifier: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Interprocedural Vulnerability Detection
items.dek: VulAgentRL uses CPG-verified evidence to detect 71.7% of real CVEs requiring interprocedural analysis; RL policy learns via teacher distillation.
items.unproven: generalization to codebases and vulnerability types outside training distribution; scalability to production codebases larger than test set.

items.title: CDN Tsunami: Exploiting HTTP/3-HTTP/1.1 Conversion for DoS Attacks
items.dek: HTTP/3 to HTTP/1.1 conversion at CDNs enables bandwidth and connection amplification DoS; measured on Tranco Top 1M.
items.unproven: whether measured CDNs have deployed patches; attack cost and detectability in practice; applicability to HTTP/3-HTTP/3 deployments.

items.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents
items.dek: StealthBench measures operational-security failures in autonomous red-team agents across 14 scenarios; agents leak credentials and destroy resources despite successful exploitation.
items.unproven: 11 hand-verified OPSEC incidents expanded into 14 dockerized tasks; whether findings transfer to agents operating against live infrastructure or sophisticated detection untested

items.title: Tailscale didn't stop the Hugging Face intrusion
items.dek: Hugging Face intrusion proceeded despite Tailscale deployment, indicating VPN alone insufficient for supply-chain protection.
items.unproven: whether Tailscale was misconfigured, what the actual attack vector was, or how this generalizes beyond this incident

items.title: Emerging Challenges in Threat Modeling for GenAI-Augmented Systems: A View from the Trenches
items.authors: Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra et al.
items.dek: Three threat-modeling methods applied to GenAI systems in SME; gaps identified in supply-chain and human-centered risk categories.
items.unproven: generalizability beyond single case study; maturity and adoption readiness of methods for application-security teams

items.title: Old Tricks, New Models: How Simple Image Transformations Break Modern AI-based Content Moderation
items.dek: Simple image transformations—color inversion, grayscale, rotation—bypass three commercial multimodal content-moderation APIs at scale.
items.unproven: Black-box evaluation of public APIs only; does not establish whether this reflects architectural flaws or tuning gaps in the reader's own deployment.

items.title: Benign on Label, Malicious by Design: Clean-Label Dormant-to-Activated Backdoor via Machine Unlearning with Removable Camouflage
items.dek: Machine unlearning can activate dormant clean-label backdoors injected at training time, bypassing post-training detection.
items.unproven: whether the attack survives standard model quantization, pruning, or other deployment optimizations; transferability across model families.

items.title: ThreatForest: Multi-Agent Attack Tree Generation with Pluggable TTP Framework Mapping
items.dek: Multi-agent system generates attack trees and maps steps to MITRE ATT&CK; embedding accuracy is the bottleneck, not orchestration.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to seven application domains; no comparison to manual threat modeling or existing automated tools; single sentence-transformer embedding may not generalize across architectures

items.title: MemSecBench: Tracking Agent Memory Poisoning from Persistence to Consequence and Repair
items.dek: MemSecBench benchmark tracks malicious instruction persistence, recall, and repair across 310 cases in agent memory systems with diverse backends.
items.unproven: Lab environment with controlled agent harness; behavior of memory poisoning under production deployment conditions and agent-specific drift not measured.

items.title: HoF-Bench: Rediscovering Real AI-Discovered CVEs Without Frontier Models
items.dek: Benchmark of 95 real AI-discovered CVEs shows small open-weight models rediscover 68% of vulnerabilities; frontier models detect none.
items.unproven: Eight repositories and vulnerability types may not represent distribution of exploitable defects in the reader's codebase; generalization to non-open-source codebases unclear.

items.title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation
items.dek: Three-class detector distinguishes humans, bots, and browser-automation agents; binary classifiers misroute 34–39% of agents as human.
items.unproven: Controlled benchmark with synthetic evasion; effectiveness against production traffic patterns, distributed agent behaviors, and adaptive mimicry of human cursor dynamics not established.

items.title: Borrowed Strength: Best-of-N Search over a Code EncodingBreaks Self-Check Jailbreak Defenses
items.dek: Code encoding plus best-of-N search bypasses SAGE self-check jailbreak defense, reaching 67% attack success on open models.
items.unproven: whether defense-aware retraining closes the gap; applicability to production-hardened or proprietary model guards.

items.title: Collusion with Competitive Marginals: Price-Level Audits Are Blind by Construction
items.dek: LLM agents show residual bid correlation despite individual competitive pricing, defeating single-agent price audits by design.
items.unproven: measurement limited to 20 models from 19 developers; generalization to production trading systems and defense feasibility untested

items.title: RAGuard: A Layered Defense Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems Against Data Poisoning
items.dek: RAGuard layered defense mitigates corpus poisoning in RAG systems via adversarial retriever tuning and label-free leave-one-out filtering.
items.unproven: evaluation on synthetic poisoned Natural Questions; defense against natural or adaptive poisoning, and efficacy in production retrieval corpora unknown

items.title: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages
items.dek: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption extended to arbitrary message length; theoretical contribution without deployment path.
items.unproven: no evidence of practical implementation or comparison to existing key material protection schemes; no timeline for quantum hardware capable of the required operations

items.title: Optimal T Counts under Sparsity: from QROM to State Preparation and Block Encoding
items.dek: Optimal T-count bounds for sparse quantum read-only memory scale as Θ(√sm + √sn), matching lower bounds.
items.unproven: no experimental validation on quantum hardware; theoretical result only

noise.title: Agent Skill to Force Docs in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English
noise.dek: GitHub repository adds agent skill to produce simplified technical English; tool development not tied to SAST/DAST/SCA or SDLC process.

noise.title: Show HN: Open-source engine running Gemma 4 26B in 2 GB RAM on any M-series Mac
noise.dek: TurboFieldfare runs 4-bit Gemma 4 26B on 2 GB RAM by streaming experts from SSD; on-device inference optimization technique.
noise.unproven: single model and hardware platform; does not establish whether technique applies to other MoE models or architectures

noise.title: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations
noise.dek: Anthropic documents three real-world cybersecurity incidents found during AI model evaluations; incident taxonomy adds vocabulary, no immediate tooling change.
noise.unproven: No disclosure of which evaluations, what findings changed in practice, or whether incidents apply to agents entering SDLC processes.
